feedback: Approve. This candidate is the best raced design (iteration 5, entityR2B, score 201.98: sensor x = ±0.032 m, footprint 0.016 m, kp 3.0, ki 0.30, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.5, last_direction) with one change, kd 0.30 to 0.40. The evidence behind it is iteration 5's oval steering_oscillation of 0.264, which is above the 0.25 warning level, while s-bend (0.141) and slalom (0.143) oscillation stayed low. Oval finishes were 7 of 20 and oval max_error was 0.0599, just under the 0.06 limit. Raising kd is the damping step the earlier guidance set for this case. The weights stay antisymmetric and every other value is held, so the change is single-variable and valid. I make no claim about how it will perform. The s-bend and slalom still go off track in every run (progress 0.18 and 0.11), so they are the next target after this race. Read the race as follows. If oval steering_oscillation falls below about 0.25 and oval finishes stay at 7 or more, keep kd 0.40. Then test base_speed 1.3 alone, because the s-bend and slalom failures may be speed or corner-entry limited and speed has not been varied at this sensor spread. If oval oscillation stays above 0.25 or finishes drop below 7, the extra damping is slowing the correction, so return to kd 0.30 and set kd 0.35 instead. If max_error on the oval rises above 0.06, return kp and kd to 3.0 and 0.30 and keep the spread.
requested_changes: If oval steering_oscillation falls below about 0.25 and oval finishes stay at 7 or more, keep kd 0.40 and test base_speed 1.3 alone, since the s-bend (progress 0.18) and slalom (progress 0.11) failures have not been tested against speed at the ±0.032 m spread.

If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.25 or oval finishes drop below 7 of 20, return kd to 0.30 and try kd 0.35, since iteration 5 showed the ±0.032 m spread reached 7 finishes at kd 0.30 and a larger step may over-damp the tightest oval bends.

If oval max_error rises above 0.06, return kp to 3.0 and kd to 0.30 and keep x = ±0.032 m, since kp 3.5 at the narrower spread (iteration 2, score 99.25) and ki 0.60 (iteration 4, score 103.99) both lowered the score.
